summary: Make targets for the runtime lifecycle (up/down/logs/seed on top of the existing test/verify) plus a `make dev` fast-iteration overlay (docker-compose.dev.yml) so ordinary Django/React edits don't require an image rebuild.

task_notes.RT-003: Makefile: `up`/`down`/`logs` wrap the base compose file (still a full --build every time, unchanged authoritative path); `seed` wraps the existing seed_acceptance_identities management command. docker-compose.dev.yml (opt-in via `make dev`, not auto-loaded): bind-mounts src/api into app/worker and runs uvicorn with --reload; adds a `web` service (plain node:24-slim image, no custom Dockerfile) running the Vite dev server with HMR, proxying /api to the app service via VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET. `make dev-build` covers Dockerfile/dependency changes. Added the `dev` script to src/web/package.json and a server.proxy in vite.config.ts (falls back to localhost:8080 for a bare `pnpm dev` outside Compose). README documents the fast vs. authoritative commands.

verification.command: uv run --frozen ruff format --check / ruff check / pytest / manage.py check
uvicorn --reload (host venv) + edit core/views.py while running + curl
verification.result: edit picked up live without a process restart, then reverted
200 {"status":"ok"} — proxy forwards to Django exactly as the containerized web service will (target swapped to http://app:8000)

escalations: The containerized `web` dev service's `pnpm install` step (and any `make dev-build`) needs npm-registry/PyPI access from inside Docker, which this sandbox does not have (see RT-002 receipt) — could not run `make dev` or `make dev-build` end-to-end here. Verified the underlying mechanics (uvicorn --reload, Vite proxy/HMR) directly against the host venv/node instead.
